canonical_question: Does the reported lattice misfit δ of -0.33% for CMSX-2 represent a specific value at room temperature or the service temperature of 982 °C?

question_variants.question: Does the reported lattice misfit δ of -0.33% for CMSX-2 represent a specific value at room temperature or the service temperature of 982 °C?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper cites the lattice misfit δ of CMSX-2 as -0.33% but does not specify whether this value was measured at room temperature or at the service temperature of 982 °C.

answers.answer: The text states 'Since the δ of CMSX-2 was reported around −0.33% [45]', but the evidence spans do not specify the temperature (room temperature or 982 °C) at which this value was reported.
answers.boundary_limitation: Temperature of the reported misfit value is not specified in the text.
evidence_spans: In present study, the high temperature tensile and creep behaviors of a novel alloy named high entropy superalloy (HESA) [13] have been investigated.
HESA is strengthened by the coherent L1 2 γ′ precipitates, while the FCC matrix remains high entropy (ΔS mix > 1.5 R) [14] .
For example, the composition of HESA in current study is Ni 47.9 Al 10.2 Co 16.9 Cr 7.4 Fe 8.9 Ti 5.8 Mo 0.9 Nb 1.2 W 0.4 C 0.4 (at%), so the calculated ΔS mix is 1.60 R
